case_name: Mahesh Ram v. State Of Himachal Pradesh And Others

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Himachal Pradesh and Others

facts_of_case: Petitioner was appointed as Carpenter/Foreman in 1973. He solemnised marriage with Ms. Kamlesh Devi in 1994, but no child was born. He then solemnised second marriage with Ms. Jawala Devi, younger sister of Ms. Kamlesh Devi. After death of his first wife in 2020, he filed representation to change nominee in pension record and enter name of Ms. Jawala Devi instead.

legal_principles.principle: A presumption of a valid marriage can be drawn if a man and woman cohabit continuously for a long spell.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Apex Court observed that if a man and woman cohabited continuously for a long spell, one can draw a presumption in favour of a valid marriage.
cited_cases: Shiramabai and Others Vs. The Captain Record Officer and Another, Civil Appeal (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the one who seeks to deprive a relationship of its legal origin to prove that no marriage had taken place.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Apex Court further held that this presumption is rebuttable, though heavy onus is placed on the one who seeks to deprive the relationship of its legal origin to prove that no marriage had taken place.
cited_cases: Shiramabai and Others Vs. The Captain Record Officer and Another, Civil Appeal (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: Issue a writ of mandamus directing the Respondent authorities to enter the name of the second wife of the petitioner in the pension record.
